Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human
 Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.
This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.
 The role
 Okta enables universal, secure access to technology for every user and organization. Okta Customer Identity (OCI) is the identity platform behind that promise for the applications our customers build for their own customers: the login, MFA, and account management layer for millions of end users across B2B, B2B2C and B2C products. OCI sits alongside Okta Workforce Identity (OWI) as one of the two halves of the Okta platform.
 We're hiring a Senior Product Manager to grow OCI's footprint inside our existing enterprise base and to incubate the next generation of platform capabilities. This is a builder's role. You'll spend a good chunk of your time in true zero-to-one territory: sizing a raw opportunity, proving it out with a design partner or two, and turning it into a capability that ships and gets adopted. You'll spend the rest of it as the connective tissue across engineering, design, research, and go-to-market, making sure those bets land in the field.
 What you will own
 New Capability Incubation: Own the pipeline of zero-to-one bets on the Okta’s Okta Customer Identity platform, from a rough problem statement through a validated design and a shipped v1. You'll decide what's worth building before anyone asks engineering to build it.
 Platform Growth: Drive the product side of Okta Customer Identity platform expansion into our existing enterprise base. You'll turn a hypothesis about why they haven't adopted the Okta Customer Identity platform into product changes that remove the reason.
 Cross-functional Delivery: Be the person engineering, design, research, and go-to-market call when a new Okta Customer Identity platform capability needs a decision. You'll write the specs, run the reviews, and keep a dozen loosely connected workstreams moving toward the same launch.
 A day in the life
 Your day splits between zero-to-one thinking and shipping discipline. You might start the morning studying churn or expansion data for a segment we don't serve well yet, trying to figure out whether the gap is a feature gap or a positioning gap. An hour later you're on a call with a design partner customer, walking through a rough prototype and taking notes on what confused them.
 By midday you're in execution mode: reviewing a spec with your engineering lead, debating whether a capability needs its own data model or can extend an existing one, and pushing back on scope that's grown past what the opportunity actually justifies. You write plainly. Your specs read like an explanation to a smart colleague, not a wish list.
 In the afternoon you sync with go-to-market and your PMM partner on how a capability in progress should be positioned once it ships, and you flag anything that changes the pitch. You close the day presenting to a customer or prospect, walking them through what's shipped and what's coming on the roadmap. 
 Responsibilities
 Identify, size, and validate new zero-to-one opportunities on the Okta Customer Identity platform, using customer conversations, usage data, and market signals rather than internal opinion alone.
 Define and execute a roadmap that balances new capability bets against platform reliability, security hardening, and performance
 Write clear, detailed specs and requirements that give engineering and design unambiguous direction, especially in areas with no existing playbook.
 Partner with sales, customer success, and product marketing to turn a shipped capability into an adopted one, including understanding why customers who should adopt haven't.
 Track the CIAM market and competitive moves from Auth0, Microsoft, and Ping, and use that context to sharpen where the Okta Customer Identity platform should and shouldn't compete.
 Be the go-to expert for your area of the Okta Customer Identity platform roadmap in front of customers, executives, and cross-functional partners.
 Required
 5+ years of product management experience in enterprise SaaS, platform products, or identity and access management, with at least one zero-to-one launch you can speak to end to end.
 A track record of building and executing a strategy that spans multiple teams, and delivering on it, not just presenting it.
 Strong written and verbal communication. You can write a spec an engineer can build from and a one-pager an executive can act on, without changing the substance between the two.
 Strong analytical and decision-making skills. You can build a credible plan from incomplete or conflicting inputs, and explain the assumptions behind it.
 BS in Computer Science, Business, or an equivalent background, with the ability to hold your own in a design review with engineering and architecture.
 Preferred
 Experience with Customer Identity and Access Management 
 Experience partnering with sales or customer success on an attach or expansion motion, not just a net-new sales motion.
 Public speaking experience, ideally in front of customers or at industry events.
 MBA or equivalent graduate business degree.
 Top 3 qualities we are hiring for
 Zero-to-one conviction: You've taken a fuzzy opportunity from "should we even do this?" to a shipped, adopted capability, without a playbook telling you how. You know the difference between not validated yet and not going to work, and you don't confuse the two.
 Decisive action in the dark : You rarely have perfect data or complete requirements. You confidently make high-stakes calls using a mix of telemetry, customer anecdotes, and sharp product intuition. You explicitly name your assumptions, move fast, and revise them in public without ego when new information arrives.
 Unquestioned influence : You lead without relying on a reporting structure. You naturally align engineering, design, GTM, and the field behind your understanding of the customer. You are the definitive, credible voice of the product in CISO boardrooms and internal executive reviews.
 **You must attend in person orientation physically in the Toronto office on the first Tuesday of employment.
**You must go physically into the Toronto office 2 days a week.

 Make our brands the most loved and trusted pet brands in North America, not just the most bought.  Better Everyday : review every brand moment against its goal, and make the next one bigger, cheaper or better.

 COMPANY OVERVIEW 
 Salt is a North American marketing agency that creates connected experiences through creative, digital & media innovation. 
 Our mission is to “Earn The World’s Attention” and Salt is built to find, develop, execute, and amplify the ideas that are worthy of our clients’ audiences. We’ve structured our agency to do what’s right for our clients – to connect different perspectives, to work across mediums, and to focus on delivering meaningful, effective results.

 As an Account Supervisor, you’ll oversee a portfolio of mid-sized client accounts or multiple brands within a larger partnership, operating in a fast-paced, client-facing environment. You are both a trusted advisor to clients and a day-to-day leader for your team, balancing hands-on delivery with coaching and oversight. 
 You’ll manage relationships, budgets, and cross-functional execution, ensuring every campaign phase delivers measurable value against client goals. You’ll proactively identify opportunities, risks, or efficiencies, bringing clarity and structure to complex, multi-channel programs. 
 With a balance of strategic thinking, sharp communication, and calm problem-solving, you’ll lead integrated teams through shifting priorities with confidence and composure. Whether guiding junior colleagues, managing vendors, or preparing client strategies, you’ll bring initiative, adaptability, and integrity to every interaction—helping teams deliver great work from idea to execution.

 Project & Operational Management 
 Independently manage a portfolio of projects and workstreams, ensuring delivery across all phases of execution. 
 Own timelines, approvals, and cross-functional coordination to keep integrated campaigns on track. 
 Lead internal meetings, project schedules, and operational activities across the account lifecycle. 
 Anticipate needs and proactively address risks, adapting plans to shifting priorities while maintaining composure. 
 Identify and implement process improvements that increase efficiency, delivery quality, and team effectiveness.

 Manage contracts, negotiations, and performance to ensure accountability and high-quality delivery.

 Provide oversight, direction, and coaching to team members and on-site staff, fostering morale and professional growth.

 client briefs, and strategic proposals to support new business and retention efforts.

 An overview of this role 
 Support Engineering at GitLab believes that healthy teams deliver a healthy customer experience, and that command during a crisis shouldn't fall to whoever happens to be senior and available. GitLab's global Incident & Escalation Management (IM/EM) function coordinates critical incidents, complex multi-team engagements, and executive-level escalations for enterprise customers. As Escalation Manager, you'll own complex, executive, and commercial escalations where customer trust and the relationship are at stake, alongside or independently of a technical issue.
 In this functional role, you'll advocate for customers inside GitLab, coordinate teams toward resolution, and lead relationship repair after the event.
 What you'll do 
 Own complex, executive, and commercial escalations end-to-end, as defined in GitLab's IM/EM engagement model.
 Advocate for customers internally and coordinate Engineering, Support, Product, Customer Success, and Sales toward resolution, tracking commitments and holding owning teams accountable to agreed dates and deliverables.
 Maintain a written, customer-facing resolution plan from engagement through confirmed resolution, updating it at each communication milestone.
 Coordinate with Incident Managers during concurrent technical incidents to maintain a single, coherent narrative for the customer.
 Own external escalation communications using GitLab's approved templates and cadence, and represent GitLab in high-stakes customer conversations where clarity and ownership influence retention.
 Engage Sales, Customer Success, and executive stakeholders as needed, including executive-to-executive communication for Severity 1 and 2 events. Brief GitLab leadership with concise summaries that distinguish what's known, what's unknown, and next steps.
 Lead post-escalation reviews and relationship repair plans, contribute corrective actions with named owners and due dates to postmortems, and hand the relationship back to the account's Customer Success Manager at resolution.
 Partner with the Head of IM/EM to develop playbooks, communication templates, and process improvements based on patterns from escalations.
 What you'll bring 
 Experience in enterprise technical support, customer success, or incident and escalation management at a business-to-business software-as-a-service or enterprise software company.
 A track record of owning complex, multi-stakeholder escalations end-to-end, including executive customer engagements and structured resolution or account plans.
 Executive-level written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical detail into plain-language updates for customers and GitLab leadership.
 The ability to coordinate Engineering, Support, Product, Customer Success, and Sales under pressure without formal authority over those teams.
 Calm, structured decision-making with incomplete information and the ability to provide a steadying presence in high-stress customer situations.
 Proficiency with support and coordination tools such as Zendesk, Salesforce, Slack, and PagerDuty, or equivalent platforms.
 Availability for on-call coverage supporting executive escalations as part of a globally distributed team.
 Nice to have: Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL) Foundation or equivalent certification; customer-facing experience with GitLab, development, security, and operations (DevSecOps), continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), or cloud-native products; experience with formal escalation or incident command frameworks; or AI-assisted support tools for triage, sentiment analysis, or resolution drafting.

Media buying is now the easy part. 
 In 2026, the buying itself is piping. The levers that actually move a DTC account are creative, offer, and conversion rate, and the platform keeps getting better at rewarding whoever gets those right.
 So we don't hire media buyers. We hire marketers who buy media.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands across our service lines, 20 to 25 of them on paid media, and we spend $6-9M a month on Meta. We're hiring one person to own a handful of those accounts end to end.
 Here's what "end to end" actually means here.
 You are the account manager. We don't have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership and accountability: when you're the person answering for the account, it's your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You are the creative strategist. You do the research, you find the angles, and you write the briefs and the scripts. You direct our editors and designers rather than filing requests with them. Creative isn't a ticket you submit. It's your job.
 You build the things the account needs. If conversion rate is the bottleneck, you build the landing page. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You carry up to six accounts. That's the capacity we run at today, and the team averages about four and a half. You'll manage far fewer accounts than you would at most agencies. In exchange you get real ownership of the results and you get to work as an end to end marketer instead of one station on an assembly line.
 You can live anywhere. We're a remote team and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you're the client's point of contact and there's nobody else to cover it. The rest of your day is yours.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we'll both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 We're growing fast and we keep the bar high. 
 We believe the best media buyer today is a sharp marketer who uses AI every day. We built an internal creative analysis tool that connects to Claude, and we use Pipeboard to read and write to ad accounts and run heavy analysis. You don't need to know our stack yet. You do need to actually use AI in your work, not be afraid of it, and teach yourself what you don't know.
 What the job looks like
 Own 4 to 6 DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, the creative lead, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $30k/mo to $1M/mo.
 Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you're the one who answers when something isn't working.
 Run the research before the ads. Marketing is 80% research here. You mine customer reviews, ad comments, support tickets, and Reddit for the language and objections that become angles. You pull competitor ad libraries. You run our internal tooling that OCRs and transcribes the ads in your account and ties them to performance, so you know what winning and losing actually look like in this account.
 Write the briefs and the scripts, and direct the work. Creative direction is yours. You run revision rounds with our editors and designers and you hold the quality bar.
 Ship creative on a cadence. Roughly 8 to 10 new ad launches a week is where accounts hold, in batches every 1 to 1.5 weeks. Informed volume, not spray and pray. We want better hypotheses, not more randomness.
 Build and test landing pages. Advertorials, comparison pages, PDPs. Built in Claude Code, deployed to Vercel, tested live on a subdomain before anything gets pushed into the client's theme.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Report on new customer economics. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended ROAS and not last click. You'll be expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.
 You're a fit if
 You've done this with real money. Hands-on Meta at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them.
 You're AI-native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude (or equivalent) as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it. If you can research, write, and build a converting page from scratch, we can teach you the buying.
 You can write direct response in English at a native or near-native level. Hooks, scripts, ad copy, advertorial. In the customer's own words, not invented. This is the single biggest source of leverage in the role and the thing we screen hardest for. If writing persuasive English isn't a strength, this isn't the job.
 You can communicate your ideas. This matters as much as anything else on this list. You'll be in front of clients constantly with nobody in between, so you need to be able to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire.
 You have taste and you know when to hand off. You direct creative, you don't half-build it yourself. AI slop shipped to a client is a habit we break, not a shortcut we accept.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you've built or operated your own Shopify store or eComm brand. Several of our team have, and it shows.
 You're not a fit if
 "That wasn't my role" is in your vocabulary. It's the fastest way to end an interview here. If creative was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the creative.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 Why This Role Is Exciting
 This is not a maintenance job. You will be surrounded by people who move fast, care a lot, and take the work seriously.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets.  We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You will grow into senior strategy.  We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

L’Expérience Aviva

 Chez Aviva Canada, nous plaçons les gens au premier plan : nos employés, nos clients et nos communautés.  L’Opportunité 
En tant que spécialiste, Assurance de la qualité, vous jouerez un rôle clé pour garantir la précision, la cohérence et l’intégrité des processus d’expertise et de gestion des sinistres. Joignez-vous à notre équipe!
 Ce que vous ferez 
 Effectuer des contrôles réguliers des dossiers d’évaluation afin de s’assurer du respect des directives internes et des normes du secteur.

 Offrir de l’accompagnement et de la rétroaction aux membres de l’équipe afin d’améliorer la qualité du travail et le rendement.
 Participer à des initiatives interfonctionnelles visant à améliorer l’expérience client et l’efficacité opérationnelle.
 Ce que vous apporterez 
 Au moins trois ans d’expérience en sinistres automobiles, en expertise ou en assurance de la qualité.

 Solide connaissance des principes de l’assurance, des plateformes d’estimation (p. ex. Audatex et Mitchell) ainsi que des exigences réglementaires.

 Excellentes aptitudes en communication et en relations interpersonnelles. 
 Capacité à travailler de façon autonome et en collaboration dans un environnement au rythme soutenu.
 Maîtrise des outils Microsoft 365 (Excel, Teams et SharePoint).
 Connaissance du français necessaire
 Maîtrise de l’anglais de niveau intermédiaire avancé est exigée en raison de la nature des tâches, des outils de travail ou des interactions avec des partenaires, des membres de l’équipe ou des clients anglophones.​

 Titre de PAA ou autre titre professionnel spécifique au secteur de l’assurance.
 Expérience des plateformes d’estimation numériques, notamment Mitchell, ou de plateformes similaires.

Notre environnement de travail axé sur le numérique, combiné à nos bureaux et espaces de travail collaboratifs bien situés, offre à notre équipe la liberté et la flexibilité de travailler de la façon qui la rend la plus productive.
 À propos de nous 
 Tecsys est un innovateur en pleine croissance offrant des solutions de chaîne d'approvisionnement aux principaux systèmes de santé, hôpitaux et entreprises pharmaceutiques, ainsi qu'aux distributeurs, détaillants et fournisseurs de services logistiques tiers (3PL). L'équipe Infrastructure et opérations de production s'efforce de tout automatiser, gère notre infrastructure en tant que code (infrastructure as code) et bâtit notre plateforme à partir d'outils et d'applications open source.
 Responsabilités 
 Construire et automatiser les déploiements d'infrastructure client.
 Concevoir des solutions évolutives de déploiement, d'intégration et de livraison continues (CI/CD) et d'automatisation à l'échelle du cycle de vie de la plateforme Tecsys.
 Tirer parti d'agents d'intelligence artificielle (Amazon Kiro) pour orchestrer et accélérer les tâches techniques, tout en validant les résultats.
 Développer la logique de déploiement, les tests automatisés et les playbooks de réponse aux incidents.
 Gérer l'infrastructure AWS/Azure, les architectures hybrides, Kubernetes et les environnements de conteneurs.
 Surveiller la stabilité de la plateforme, résoudre les incidents et participer au support d'astreinte (on-call).
 Collaborer avec les équipes de développement sur l'automatisation des déploiements et l'évolutivité de l'infrastructure.
 Planifier et exécuter des initiatives de maintenance et d'amélioration continue.

 Baccalauréat ou expérience équivalente.
 4 ans et plus d'expérience dans le soutien de systèmes de production Java/.NET à haut volume et haute disponibilité.

 Expérience avec des outils CI/CD tels que GitLab ou Jenkins.
 Expérience avec des outils de surveillance et d'observabilité tels que CloudWatch, Datadog, New Relic ou Nagios.
 Excellente maîtrise de l'anglais, à l'oral comme à l'écrit, essentielle pour assurer une communication efficace avec les clients, fournisseurs, partenaires d'affaires et collègues à l'extérieur du Québec.

Cependant, nous demandons que toutes les informations que vous fournissez reflètent votre expérience réelle, et que toute évaluation ou tout document écrit soumis représente votre propre travail et votre propre réflexion.

Une conversation authentique et directe nous aide à mieux comprendre votre façon de penser, de collaborer et de communiquer.  The Schulich School of Music of McGill University is Canada’s leading institution for the professional training of performers and composers, and the humanities-based and scientific research in music and sound. We seek individuals with an international profile in music performance and research who will maintain a high level of professional activity and are able to teach and supervise students in all university degree and diploma programs through to the doctoral level. Montreal offers a vibrant multicultural living environment and is consistently rated among the best student cities in the world. 
 The Department of Performance invites applications from accomplished brass instrumentalists for a tenure-track position in Brass at the rank of Assistant Professor, beginning August 1, 202 7. We seek an accomplished brass instrumentalist with a specialization in trumpet, although outstanding candidates whose primary expertise is in trombone, horn, or tuba are also encouraged to apply. The appointment will be for an initial three-year term. Appointment at the rank of Associate Professor may be considered for an exceptional candidate.
 Job Duties: 
Academic responsibilities include teaching, research, and service to the University. The successful candidate will be expected to maintain an active international profile with a high level of professional activity, while teaching and supervising students at the undergraduate, graduate, and diploma levels, including those preparing for professional careers. The position also involves supervision of doctoral students in brass performance as a member of doctoral advisory committees. Teaching responsibilities will include applied instruction and chamber music coaching and may also encompass courses and seminars related to the candidate’s area of expertise, such as brass literature, orchestral excerpts, performance practice, pedagogy, or other specialized topics. Service responsibilities will include leadership and coordination of the Brass Area and may involve participation in departmental and School committees, as well as contributions to curriculum development and program enhancement. The successful candidate must demonstrate the ability to develop and sustain a level of artistic activity and/or research consistent with the University's expectations for tenure.
 Qualifications and Education Requirements: 
A doctorate or equivalent professional experience, together with a distinguished international reputation as a performer, is required. The successful candidate will demonstrate excellence in teaching students at the highest levels of performance and scholarship, broad knowledge of the brass repertoire, and a strong commitment to fostering an inclusive, equitable, and supportive learning environment. The candidate will also contribute to student recruitment and outreach initiatives that engage and inspire emerging musicians. Exceptional leadership, organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills are essential, as is the ability to collaborate effectively with colleagues, students, and the broader musical community.

Salary and rank commensurate with qualifications and experience. The position is subject to final budgetary approval.

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked. 
 That is the whole job.
 Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
 So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
 You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
 Here is what "end to end" actually means.
 You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
 You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 What the job looks like 
 Own a set of DTC accounts  as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
 Own the client relationship.  There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
 Audit before you touch anything.  Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
 Run brand and non brand as different businesses.  Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
 Know what PMax is actually doing.  The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
 Keep Google's automation on a leash.  Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
 Own the feed.  Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
 Own the tracking.  GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.  Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Build the things the account needs.  Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
 You are a fit if 
 You have done this with real money.  Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
 You are fluent in the whole stack , not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
 You are AI native, and you build.  This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
 You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.  You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
 You are skeptical of your own numbers.  You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.  Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
 You are not a fit if 
 "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
 Why this role is exciting 
 This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

 About the role 
 At Clutch, we believe advances in AI are fundamentally changing how great products are built. Traditional handoffs between product, design, and engineering are giving way to smaller, faster teams where builders can take ideas from concept to production in days instead of months.
 As a Senior Data Engineer, you'll own the data platform that powers decision-making across Clutch, from how we buy and price vehicles, to how customers move through our funnel, to how we deliver and finance cars. The pipelines, models, and infrastructure you build will be the foundation our analysts and data scientists rely on every day, including for our fast-growing financial services work.
 Our data engineers don't just move data, they own outcomes. That means working directly with stakeholders to understand what they need, designing systems that scale with the business, and making sure the data behind every important decision is reliable, well-modeled, and easy to use. If you see a broken pipeline or a question the data can't answer yet and feel compelled to fix it, you'll thrive at Clutch.
 Technology at Clutch 
 We believe great engineers can learn great technology.
 Our data team builds with technologies like Snowflake, dbt, Airflow, Python, and AWS, alongside an application stack of TypeScript, PostgreSQL, and Express. We're far more interested in exceptional engineers than perfect technology matches. If you've built outstanding data platforms in another modern stack and are excited to learn, improve, and help evolve ours, we'd love to talk.
 What you'll do 
 Own Clutch's data platform end-to-end, designing and evolving the architecture behind our warehouse, pipelines, and data models with long-term scalability in mind.
 Build reliable, well-tested ELT pipelines that bring together data from our applications, operational systems, and third-party tools.
 Design data models in partnership with analysts and data scientists so that trusted, well-structured data is easy to find and use across the business.
 Build the data foundations for our financial services work, partnering closely with the data scientist focused on that area to support modeling, experimentation, and analytics.
 Own data quality and observability, with monitoring, testing, and alerting that catch issues before stakeholders do.
 Apply strong DevOps practices to data, including version control, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, and automated deployments.
 Use AI as part of your everyday engineering workflow to prototype, accelerate development, and improve code quality.
 Make thoughtful technical decisions that balance speed, cost, quality, and maintainability, and continuously evaluate new tools that help the team move faster.
 Establish data standards, documentation, and governance practices as our platform matures.
 Mentor others and raise the bar for data engineering across the team through design discussions and code reviews.

 Have built and operated production data pipelines and platforms that people rely on.
 Advanced SQL and strong programming skills in Python (TypeScript is a plus).
 Hands-on experience with a modern cloud data warehouse such as Snowflake, BigQuery, or Redshift.
 Experience with transformation and orchestration tools such as dbt and Airflow.
 Experience with cloud platforms, ideally AWS, and their data services.
 Strong data modeling skills, including designing for analytics use cases.
 Experience with DevOps and observability tooling such as Git, GitHub Actions, Docker, Terraform, and Datadog.
 Use AI as a force multiplier to explore ideas, prototype solutions, and accelerate development.
 Enjoy working directly with stakeholders to understand problems and deliver business value.
 Communicate clearly and are comfortable making decisions in ambiguous environments.
 Care as much about business outcomes as technical excellence.

 Experience supporting data science or ML workflows in production.

 About the role 
 We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated Manager, Cybersecurity Governance and Compliance to join our cybersecurity team. Reporting to the Director of Governance, Risk and Compliance, this role will lead the transformation of IFC’s traditional Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) capabilities into a threat intel driven, governance, compliance and risk advisory function.  
 With your strong technical understanding, leadership skills, and innovative mindset, you will help shape the future of IFC’s cybersecurity practices, strengthen collaboration across Technology and Cyber teams, and lead the team through a transformation of its mandate, organization, capabilities, and ways of working.  
 What you'll do here:   
 Lead and manage a team of cybersecurity professionals responsible for technical risk advisory, security practices, governance, control effectiveness, and security issue management.  
 Lead the transformation of the team from a traditional GRC function into a technically oriented security risk advisory practice; including an uplift of the security standards, policies and guidelines.   
 Define and implement the team’s future operating model, including its roles, responsibilities, processes, engagement model, and interaction with security and technology teams.  
 Lead the evaluation and challenge of cybersecurity remediation by assessing risks and findings from threat profiling, red-team exercises, audits, incidents, and other assurance activities; validating that proposed solutions and timelines appropriately address risk; and strengthening mechanisms to track, report, escalate, and confirm timely closure.  
 Develop and maintain practical cybersecurity governance processes that enable sound risk-based decision-making while avoiding unnecessary administrative or compliance-driven activities.  
 Provide advice and constructive challenge in support of the security function on financial compliance requirements, with strong familiarity with frameworks such as NI 52-109 and SOX.  
 Drive continuous improvement of IFC’s security controls and practices by identifying systemic weaknesses, recurring issues, and opportunities to improve design, implementation, and operational effectiveness.  
 Coordinate maturity assessments, independent assurance activities, and other security reviews, ensuring that findings are translated into actionable and measurable improvements.  
 Maintain appropriate alignment with applicable regulatory requirements, internal policies, risk-management expectations, and industry practices, while keeping the team’s primary focus on effective cybersecurity risk reduction; respond to regulatory and third-party information requests and audits.   
 Prepare and present meaningful metrics, insights and reports to senior management, highlighting significant risks, remediation progress, risk acceptance decisions, recurring themes, and areas requiring management attention.  
 Lead the evolution of the team’s capabilities by identifying required technical skills, hiring new employees, planning training and development for existing employees, and supporting the reassignment of employees whose skills are not aligned with the future operating model.  
 Introduce innovative approaches, tools, and technologies to improve the efficiency, quality, and impact of technical risk advisory and security-practice activities.  
 Ensure the team has the expertise, resources, processes, and stakeholder relationships required to support the Technology and Cyber mission.  
 What you bring to the table:   
 Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information technology, cybersecurity, or any combination of equivalent education and experience.  
 Minimum of ten (10) years of experience in information technology or cybersecurity, including at least three (3) years managing technical or cybersecurity teams.  
 Strong knowledge of cybersecurity principles, security architecture, vulnerability management, application and infrastructure security, cloud security, threat and risk assessment, and security-control effectiveness.  
 Demonstrated experience evaluating cybersecurity findings and advising on appropriate remediation strategies, accountable owners, compensating controls, risk acceptance, and remediation timelines.  
 Experience working with findings from red team exercises, vulnerability assessments, audits, security incidents, or other technical assurance activities.  
 Experience validating whether proposed technical solutions effectively address identified security risks.  
 Experience leading organizational, operational, or capability transformations within cybersecurity, Technology, or risk-management functions.  
 Experience building or evolving a cybersecurity risk advisory, security governance, security assurance, or technical risk-management practice.  
 Experience developing team operating models, defining roles and responsibilities, hiring talent, and building technical capabilities through training and employee development.  
 Knowledge of cybersecurity governance and risk frameworks and standards such as NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-53, ISO/IEC 27001, CIS Controls, or equivalent frameworks.  
 Working knowledge of regulatory and control frameworks such as OSFI B-13, OSC 52-109, and SOX.   
 Strong ability to communicate complex technical risks and security concepts clearly to technical teams, business stakeholders, and senior management.  
 Initiative, creativity, and autonomy: you proactively seek resources and information, make informed decisions, challenge ineffective practices, manage expectations, and drive continuous improvement.  
 Strong collaboration, influencing, facilitation, and relationship-management skills, with the ability to create alignment across multiple Technology, Cyber, and business teams.  
 Strong ethical principles and a sound understanding of business, technology, and information-security ethics.  
 One or more of the following certifications would be considered an asset: CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CISA, CCSP, SABSA, GIAC certifications, or other relevant technical cybersecurity certifications.

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, electricians, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers, while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want.



Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers.




THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Senior Product Designer to join our Foundations team, which is responsible for the systems, patterns, and surfaces that help us build consistent, high-quality experiences. You’ll play a key role in shaping and evolving UI components and UX patterns in Jobber’s design system across multiple platforms. This role necessarily involves thinking about how the design system operates in an evolving age of AI design and development. You’ll lead projects and initiatives that raise standards for visual and interaction design, usability, and accessibility, while improving consistency and team velocity.

Our team collaborates closely with designers, product managers, and engineers across the company. You’ll work at the intersection of design, engineering, and systems thinking to help other teams build better experiences, faster, and to turn good ideas into great experiences that are easier to build, ship, and repeat.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Lead design system projects to create and refine components, interaction patterns, and design tokens that scale across web and mobile platforms

 - Apply Jobber’s brand and experience principles to the product through thoughtful, high-quality visual and interaction design

 - Identify gaps in the system and proactively drive solutions that improve consistency and usability at scale, and raise the bar for UX quality

 - Define and evolve governance models, contribution processes, and best practices

 - Partner closely with Engineering to ensure high-quality implementation and to improve how we incorporate the system into AI-backed design and development tools and workflows

 - Collaborate with designers and product teams to support adoption, share best practices, and incorporate feedback

 - Advocate for UX quality across the company to improve visual design, interaction design, accessibility, usability, and performance

 - Contribute to a strong culture of collaboration, mentorship, feedback, and continuous improvement


TO BE SUCCESSFUL, YOU SHOULD HAVE:

 - A portfolio demonstrating your design craft, systems thinking, and measurable impact on product quality or team efficiency

 - 2–5 years experience designing and evolving design systems, including work on components, patterns, tokens, and documentation

 - A track record of leading projects or initiatives that improved design consistency and quality across a product

 - Deep expertise in interaction design, UI patterns, and visual design

 - Strong understanding of accessibility standards for the web and/or mobile and how to embed them into systems

 - Comfort collaborating closely with engineers and understanding how design translates to code

 - Familiarity with front-end technologies (HTML, CSS, and frameworks like React)

 - Experience with modern design tools like Figma (components, tokens, auto-layout, prototyping)

 - Strong proficiency in today’s evolving AI design landscape, including prototyping, shared libraries, and design documentation

 - Strong judgment in making tradeoffs that scale across teams and use cases, balancing flexibility with standardization

 - Proven ability to work cross-functionally and build alignment with designers, engineers, and product partners


BONUS POINTS

 - Experience scaling a design system in a fast-growing, multi-product environment

 - Experience designing complex software-as-a-service (SaaS) tools for business (B2B), especially for small-business customers (SMB)

 - Coding skills including experience with Typescript — ability to implement tokens and improve component quality, hands-on

 - Experience influencing strategy, aligning stakeholders, and driving adoption at scale

 - Passion for blending roles, extending design into code and vice-versa

Our Hiring Process:

You can expect the interview process to include the following steps:

 - Talent Team Interview (45 min): An introduction to Jobber, your background, and what you’re looking for.

 - Portfolio Review (60 min): A deep dive into selected projects to understand your design process, decision-making, and impact.

 - Functional Whiteboard Exercise (75 min): A collaborative problem-solving session to see how you approach ambiguity and work through complex UX challenges.

 - Cross-Functional Interview (30 min): A conversation about your approach to cross-functional collaboration, including communication, feedback, and decision-making with product and engineering partners.

Location:

We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect. To support this, the role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo.

Compensation:

At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and supportive of your experience and growth. Our salary ranges are designed to reflect the progression from learning the role to truly excelling. This role has an annual salary of:

Canada: minimum annual salary of $125,800 CAD, a midpoint of $147,900, and a maximum salary of $170,100 CAD.

We design our compensation to reflect each new hire’s skills, experience, and the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact, with fully established hires typically starting around the midpoint. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers below the midpoint reflect strong potential with room to develop. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both an individual’s current capabilities and their opportunity for future growth.

Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You’ll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.

We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we’re happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!

What you can expect from Jobber:

 - A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.

 - A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.

 - A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.

 - To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process.



A bit more about us:

Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!

Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.
 What is The Role 
 The Elastic Security Endpoint Protections team builds the visibility, prevention, and on-device machine learning capabilities at the core of Elastic Defend, our endpoint and SIEM security solution. We work in kernel and user mode across Windows, macOS, and Linux, against adversaries who study how to defeat what we build. Our work reaches the security community as well as the product, through original research and conference talks. We are looking for a Senior Manager who has done this work personally and can still review a design or write code. You will lead a globally distributed team and set the tone for a group that values candid feedback, collaborative learning, and mentorship.
 We believe security is a team sport, and our efficacy is independently verified rather than simply claimed: in recent third-party enterprise protection testing, Elastic Security earned a perfect malware protection score with zero false alarms, the top result in the field. If you are energized by leading world-class engineers and making a measurable dent in how the industry defends the endpoint, we would love to hear from you!
 What You Will Be Doing
 Lead, mentor, and grow a world-class engineering team. Guide senior research engineers across endpoint internals, prevention engineering, and machine learning. Coach career development, deliver candid feedback, own the hiring pipeline, and set new engineers up to contribute quickly.
 Own the roadmap and drive delivery. Decide where to invest in new visibility and where to deepen existing protection engines, balancing efficacy, performance, and stability across millions of endpoints. Work with product managers to define requirements and land high-quality features on release timelines.
 Connect your team's work to the rest of Elastic Security. Every event source your team adds unlocks new detection and protection capabilities across the product. Invest in the joint planning, working relationships, and shared accountability that get your team's work into customers' hands.
 Direct the team's machine learning work. Set direction on model development, training data quality, and the telemetry features those models depend on, and connect that work to the broader machine learning strategy across Elastic Security.
 Drive cross-platform protection parity. Bring the depth Elastic has on Windows to macOS and Linux, keep the team ahead of new hardware architectures, and sustain the platform vendor relationships that give you early access to emerging operating system security APIs.
 Represent the team externally. Support your engineers in presenting at conferences and publishing on Elastic Security Labs, engage with customers and partners on protection capabilities, and be a credible voice for Elastic in the endpoint security community.
 What You Bring
 People-leadership experience managing senior technical individual contributors on a globally distributed team. You lead with curiosity rather than authority, actively solicit feedback, and have a track record of growing people, not just shipping releases.
 You have been a practitioner. Substantial hands-on experience as a security researcher before moving into leadership: analyzing attacker tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs), building the protections that counter them, and shipping into software that runs on customer machines at scale.
 Operating system internals knowledge , in both kernel and user mode, earned hands-on rather than through oversight, and deep enough to reason about undocumented behavior and challenge a design on its technical merits. Windows depth is what we need most, with macOS or Linux close behind.
 Hands-on reverse engineering and malware analysis experience. You have done this work yourself, and can still read a disassembly, assess a research finding on its merits, and judge which threats warrant investment.
 An adversarial instinct. You anticipate how a protection will be evaded before it ships, and hold the team to designing for resilience rather than for the proof of concept in front of them.
 Clear communication skills , comfortable writing for technical and executive audiences and distilling deeply technical work for non-expert stakeholders.
 Motivation to thrive in a distributed, autonomous environment , with a genuine passion for protecting customers from real-world adversaries.
 Demonstrated experience leveraging AI-assisted development tools to accelerate feature development, debug complex systems, and optimize existing codebases.
 You possess the ability to comfortably rotate across projects, collaborate across functions and teams, and seamlessly adapt to evolving team structures.
 Bonus Points
 Prior ownership of an EDR, EPP, or other endpoint security product.
 Personal research output: published vulnerabilities, patents, in-depth technical writing, or conference talks.
 Experience leading machine learning engineers working on security problems.
 Experience partnering with product engineering teams to take research prototypes through to GA release.
 Conference speaking experience (e.g., Black Hat, DEF CON, CODE BLUE, Virus Bulletin).
 Familiarity with the Elastic Stack (Elasticsearch, Kibana) and Elastic Security.

 At Aviva, data is at the heart of every customer experience, business decision, and innovation journey. As a Lead Data Designer, you'll play a critical role in shaping our enterprise data landscape by defining the standards, models, and frameworks that enable trusted, secure, and reusable data across analytics, AI, and digital solutions. Working closely with business and technology partners, you'll lead end-to-end data design initiatives, apply Property & Casualty insurance expertise and industry standards such as ACORD, and help deliver scalable data solutions that support digital transformation, platform modernization, and future growth. You'll also influence how Canadian data domains align with Aviva's global data strategy while ensuring local business needs remain at the forefront.
 What you'll do 
 The Lead Data Designer establishes clear, consistent, and implementation-ready data designs across the enterprise. Key responsibilities include:
 Enterprise domain authority: Own and govern data models for assigned domains, aligning them with business capabilities, target architecture, roadmaps, and Aviva Canada’s P&C ecosystem. Resolve semantic conflicts and manage shared identifiers, classifications, reference data, hierarchies, and golden records where applicable.
 Business semantics and federated ownership: Partner with business experts, product managers, and data owners to define and drive adoption of key business concepts, critical data elements, domain boundaries, systems of record, and producer/consumer responsibilities. Ensure data models, glossaries, and contracts enable effective business, engineering, governance, and AI outcomes.
 Solution and integration modeling: Lead data design across operational stores, warehouses, data lakes/lakehouses, data products, and relational or NoSQL platforms. Apply fit-for-purpose modeling approaches and use approved logical models to support integrations, APIs, events, analytics, data science, and emerging AI consumption patterns.
 Standards, contracts, and semantic governance: Govern data modeling standards, naming conventions, and design patterns. Define and maintain data contracts covering ownership, schemas, quality, service levels, versioning, and compliance, with automated validation where appropriate. Ensure metadata, lineage, business glossaries, transformation rules, and governance controls support consistent data use across business, technology, and AI solutions.
 Migration and physical optimization: Define canonical structures, mappings, history, survivorship, validation, cutover, and transition-state designs for migration and modernization. Optimize physical models for performance, scalability, maintainability, cost, and workload patterns using partitioning, clustering, indexing, denormalization, and query optimization where appropriate.
 Privacy, security, and regulatory controls: Embed privacy and security by design, least privilege, classification, retention, masking, tokenization, and access controls. Ensure models support Canadian insurance reporting, auditability, records and evidence requirements, data residency and cross-border obligations, and insurance risk, actuarial, pricing, and capital modeling.
 AI-ready data: Design governed datasets, semantic layers, feature models, and retrieval-ready content to support AI use cases. Ensure data is trustworthy, compliant, and fit for purpose by addressing quality, lineage, provenance, privacy, security, and bias considerations. Establish clear classification and governance for structured, unstructured, and multimodal data to improve AI accuracy, traceability, and trust.
 Design assurance and conformance: Review and approve data models, schemas, APIs, and events based on established principles, risks, and trade-offs. Assess downstream impacts across data products, integrations, analytics, regulatory reporting, AI solutions, and consuming systems. Ensure implementation aligns with approved standards, document exceptions, and maintain clear decision records.
 Data Views and governance: Recognize that Data View identifies the data domains/subdomains affected and their alignment with enterprise models, standards, ownership, and governance. Over time, assume ownership of the enterprise Data View and the Solution Data View for all projects, working through architecture forums, data governance boards, stewardship councils, and roadmap planning to balance enterprise control, regulatory obligations, reuse, and federated business agility.
 Model lifecycle and observability: Manage model ownership, versioning, traceability, publication, discoverability, effective dating, change control, supersession, and retirement. After implementation, monitor adoption, semantic consistency, anomalies, schema drift, metadata and lineage completeness, data quality, contract compliance, compatibility, realized change impacts, and approved exceptions. Prioritize corrective action and continuous improvement with data owners, data-product owners, platform teams, and delivery backlogs.
 Delivery leadership: Guide and coach data, business intelligence, analytics, AI, application, architecture, engineering, delivery, and external partner teams. Balance target-state design with delivery needs, legacy constraints, and incremental modernization.
 What you'll bring 
 Experience and education: 10+ years of enterprise data modeling and design experience in large, complex organizations, including leadership of large-scale or cross-domain models. Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, Data Management, Engineering, or related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
 Enterprise modeling and governance: Expertise in conceptual, logical, and physical modeling; normalization; dimensional modeling; data vault; semantic layers; glossaries; ontologies; knowledge and context graphs; active metadata; machine-verifiable data contracts; and structured and semi-structured schemas for human, analytical, application, and AI consumers. Strong knowledge of data governance, quality, metadata, master and reference data, stewardship, lineage, retention, privacy, and security.
 Data engineering and integration: Strong SQL, data profiling, source-system and query analysis, reconciliation, and source-to-target mapping skills. Strong knowledge of ETL and ELT, batch and streaming integration, APIs, change data capture, event-driven data, and versioned API and event contracts, including ownership, backward compatibility, and schema evolution.
 Platforms and modeling tools: Experience with cloud data platforms and modern data ecosystems. Knowledge of Snowflake, AWS data services, PostgreSQL, Hadoop, Informatica, dbt, Airflow, AWS Glue, SAP PowerDesigner, ERwin Data Modeler, or comparable modeling, metadata, and lineage tools is an asset.
 Data delivery: Experience applying enterprise semantic, metadata, quality, lineage, privacy, and security practices to governed data for machine learning, generative AI, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic AI, feature engineering, and data products, including vector and embedding structures, representativeness, bias risk, and permitted-use controls.
 P&C and industry standards: Deep knowledge of Property & Casualty insurance concepts, lifecycle, terminology, and data relationships across personal and commercial lines. Ability to translate them into stable, reusable models, apply ACORD concepts, and align Canadian models with global or federated enterprise models while documenting local extensions and justified deviations.
 Decision-making and stakeholder influence: Evaluate trade-offs across performance, scalability, cost, resilience, usability, privacy, and control requirements. Apply strong facilitation, consulting, negotiation, and consensus-building skills to challenge constructively, resolve competing needs, and make timely decisions with clear evidence, rationale, and stakeholder alignment. Communicate models and decisions effectively to business experts, product and data-product owners, data stewards, risk and compliance teams, architects, engineers, AI practitioners, and senior leaders.
 Leadership and execution: Work independently, lead through influence, collaborate effectively across business, architecture, governance, and delivery teams, take accountability for outcomes, prioritize competing demands, and deliver effectively in a fast-paced environment.
 What makes you stand out

 Relevant certifications or formal learning in data management, cloud platforms, data governance, or enterprise architecture are assets, including DAMA CDMP, SnowPro, AWS, or TOGAF.

About Parallelz
 Parallelz is building a new way for mobile apps and games to reach users. Our platform turns native mobile apps into fully native web experiences in real time, with no SDK, no code changes, and no engineering lift from the developer.
 We are based in Toronto and backed by Global Founders Capital, Play Ventures, Maple VC, Two Small Fish Ventures, Weekend Fund and Garage VC amongst others.
 About the Role
 This role sits at the centre of the business and spans the functions that set our direction: corporate strategy, finance and planning, business operations, corporate development, and go-to-market. In a single quarter that might mean owning the operating model, running a pricing analysis, sizing a new market, preparing the board package, and driving a diligence work stream.
 What separates it from a traditional strategy and operations seat is how the work gets done. This is an AI-native role by design. The models, agents and automated workflows behind planning, reporting and analysis are yours to build, deploy and maintain, and the systems you put in place become how the rest of the company operates.
 You will have direct line of sight to the executive team and to the decisions that shape the company, along with real latitude to decide where your time creates the most value.
 This is a Hybrid role based in Toronto (Harbourfront Centre), with regular in-person time alongside the team.
 What You'll Do
 Partner directly with the executive team to translate strategy into operating plans, tracking execution across functions and unblocking what slows us down. Where a priority has no natural owner, you pick it up and carry it to a decision.
 Own the strategy and the analysis behind our hardest questions, from market entry and pricing through to unit economics, headcount planning and capital allocation. Frame the problem, build the model, and bring a recommendation with a number behind it.
 Own business operations across the company. Design and run the processes, systems and reporting that connect product, go-to-market, engineering and internal operations, including the vendor and partner relationships that support them, and strengthen that foundation as the business scales.
 Define where AI belongs in how the business runs. Map how work actually gets done today across product, go-to-market, finance and operations, and separate the places where AI creates real leverage from the places where it is only novelty.
 Lead adoption across the organization. Partner with function leads to redesign how work is structured rather than layering new tools onto existing processes, and manage the transition so that changes are embedded and sustained. Success here is measured by adoption and outcome, not by what was deployed.
 Support corporate development and fundraising, including investor materials, diligence, market and competitive research, and target evaluation.
 Must-Haves
 3 to 7 years in strategy and operations, business operations, chief of staff, corporate finance, or another broad cross-functional role. Backgrounds we see this working well from include management consulting, investment banking, private equity or venture, large technology companies, and high-growth startups.
 Advanced, hands-on AI fluency. You understand how these systems work under the hood and use AI extensively in your own work, automating workstreams and running persistent agents in place of manual processes. You are current by default: when something meaningful ships, you have usually already tried it.
 Quantitative depth. You are comfortable in a model and with a blank spreadsheet, and you can move between a P&L, a cohort curve and a pricing scenario without friction.
 First-principles thinking. You take a problem apart from scratch rather than pattern-matching to the last place you worked.
 Writing that moves decisions. You can turn a messy situation into a clear one-pager that gets a call made.
 Comfort with breadth. You are energised by variety, and by not knowing exactly what you will own next quarter.
 Ownership instinct. You move without waiting to be told, and you close loops.
 Nice-to-Haves
 Consumer technology, mobile, ad tech, platforms, gaming or interactive entertainment experience.
 Corporate development, M&A, venture investing, or fundraising exposure.
 Zero-to-one experience taking something of your own from idea to launch, whether that was a company, a product, or a venture you started on the side.
 Group Retirement Savings Plan matching and participation
 Comprehensive benefits package (health, dental, vision), including Health and Wellness spending account
 Generous time off policies
 Access to leading AI tools and platforms
 Parallelz is committed to building an inclusive team and welcomes applications from candidates of all backgrounds. Accommodations are available at any stage of the hiring process on request.

 At Shift Collab , we're a clinician- and women-led, award-winning national virtual mental health therapy practice of over 125 Registered Social Workers and Registered Psychotherapists reshaping virtual mental health care across Canada.
 We’re always meeting therapists who would be a great fit for our team. This is an open posting, so we’ll be collecting applications and reaching out as needed based on our current client needs. This is an independent contractor role.
 What This Role Actually Looks Like
 We invest heavily in growing your caseload through marketing, client matching, and a strong referral engine. What we need from you is a partner in that effort: someone who shows up consistently, runs excellent Meet & Greet sessions, builds strong therapeutic relationships, and keeps clients engaged in thoughtful treatment planning.
 We do the heavy lifting on visibility and operations. You focus on delivering excellent clinical care and building a caseload that lasts.
 Hours
 Typically 8 to 10 hours a week to start
 Evening and weekend availability is a strong asset
 Potential for schedule growth, based on your availability and our demand.
 What We Handle, So You Don't Have To
 Billing, scheduling, client intake admin, and back-office support are all covered. Our secure telehealth platform gives you one place to manage sessions and notes. Your time goes to clinical work and client relationships, not chasing paperwork.
 Compensation
 Our compensation model reflects clinical experience, tenure, client demand, market rates, and the full support that comes with practicing at Shift Collab. Your rate is part of a broader model that includes client referrals and matching, marketing, billing, scheduling, intake administration, technology, and ongoing practice support.
 Why Therapists Stay
 Remote work. We're remote-first, so there's no commute.
 Real professional growth. Regular workshops, webinars, and clinical training, plus access to supervision and peer groups.
 Admin and marketing support. We take care of the infrastructure behind your practice and invest in bringing new clients to Shift.
 A real community. Being 100% virtual doesn't mean practicing alone. Peer supervision, team meetings, and knowledge-sharing keep you connected.
 Your own professional presence. We help build your bio and visibility, with opportunities for some therapists to write, speak, or contribute their expertise publicly.
 Support for you, too. Wellness resources, peer support, regular touchpoints, and social events help you stay connected to the community.
 Who Thrives Here
 Therapists who:
 Approach the therapeutic relationship with engagement over acronyms
 Deliver high-quality, accessible virtual care and understand virtual-first practice
 Excel at Meet & Greet sessions and know how to turn a first conversation into a strong therapeutic match
 Take retention and treatment planning seriously so clients feel cared for and know where their therapy is going
 See caseload growth as a shared effort and are ready to actively partner on it
 Can offer some evening availability, where client demand is highest
 Want a long-term engagement, not a short-term gig
 What You Bring
 Master's in Social Work or Counselling Psychology, registered as an MSW RSW or RP
 A minimum of 2 years of post-licensure experience
 Professional liability insurance
 Reliable internet and a secure, private workspace
 Strong virtual therapy skills and comfort with telehealth platforms
 Experience or training in any of the following is a strong asset: personality disorders, workplace injuries, narcissistic abuse recovery, complex PTSD (C-PTSD), somatic or body focused therapies, anxiety, and couples therapy
 Some evening availability, ideally between 6 and 9 PM, as our clients are asking for more evening appointments. You don’t need to work only evenings to be considered
 Fluency in additional languages beyond English is a strong asset
 A genuine commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion and to working with a diverse client base
 Professional references and a Vulnerable Sector Check, required for all successful candidates
 Ready to Apply?
 This posting is open on an ongoing basis. If this sounds like your kind of fit, we’d love to hear from you. We’ll review applications as they come in and reach out as needed.
 Our Hiring Philosophy
 Our organization is deeply committed to employment equity and diversity in the workplace. We wholeheartedly welcome applications from women, members of racialized groups, visible minorities, Aboriginal persons, persons with disabilities, persons of any sexual orientation, and persons of any gender identity or gender expression.
 We are committed to ensuring that each individual has genuine, open, and unhindered access to employment opportunities within our company. Accommodations are available for applicants with disabilities throughout the recruitment process. If you require accommodations for interviews or other meetings, please let us know.
 Disclaimer
 In accordance with Ontario's Employment Standards Act, we want to be transparent about our use of artificial intelligence in this hiring process. Shift Collab uses applicant tracking software (Workable) that may include AI-assisted features to help organize, parse, and rank applications. All hiring decisions, including screening, interviewing, and final selection, are made by members of our People Operations and Clinical teams. AI is used to support our process, not to make decisions on our behalf.
